transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is... I've been having this trouble with eating lately. Once I start eating those comfort foods, I tell myself, 'Maria, that is enough,' but my hand still goes back to the pot. It's just like I can't make myself stop.
After these episodes of eating, do you feel a strong need to do something to make up for the food you consumed, such as exercising excessively, fasting, or making yourself sick?
No, I don't do any of that. I just feel awful about myself afterwards, but I don't try to make myself sick or go without food the next day. I just... I just go on, I suppose.
On average, how many times per week do these episodes of eating more than you intended occur?

Well, since my friend passed... it's been happening most weeks. I would say usually once or twice a week. It mostly happens in those quiet afternoons, you know, after I come home from choir or finish up with my gardening.
During those times when you are eating more than you intended, do you feel like you are unable to stop or control how much you are eating?

Yes, it's exactly like I mentioned when we first started talking. I really do feel like I can't stop. My mind will say, 'Maria, you have had enough,' but my hand just keeps going right back for more. Once I start eating those foods, the control is just... gone.
When you are having these episodes where you feel unable to stop eating, do you find that you are eating much more rapidly than you normally would?

Well, yes, I do. I have actually always been a pretty slow eater normally. But lately, when this happens, I eat very fast. I'll just be standing there by the kitchen counter, and... well, I'm hardly even tasting the food before the next bite is already in my mouth.
During these episodes where you eat rapidly and feel a loss of control, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Yes, I do. By the time I finally stop, my stomach just feels... tight and heavy. I usually have to go sit in my recliner and loosen my waistband because I just ate way past what actually felt comfortable.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating these large amounts of food even when you are not actually feeling physically hungry?

Well, I'm not really sure about that. I haven't really paid attention to whether my stomach is actually growling or anything before I start. I just know the urge to eat is there, but I couldn't tell you if it's because I'm truly hungry or not. I just haven't noticed.
When you think about these episodes of eating, how much do they bother you or cause you distress?

Well, I don't know if distress is the right word. I haven't really thought about it bothering me all that much. I mean... it's just something that happens. I wouldn't say it upsets me a great deal. I just haven't really paid much mind to how I feel about it, to be honest with you.
When you think back to how you feel immediately after one of these episodes, do you feel disgusted with yourself, depressed, or guilty?

Yes, I do. Afterward, I just feel... ashamed, mostly. And sad. You know, food always used to mean family and caring for my loved ones. But now, it feels like I've turned it into this secret thing that I have to hide from the people at my church. It just makes me feel awful about myself when I'm done.
Could you tell me for about how many months this pattern of eating has been happening to you?
Well, it started right after my close friend passed away... so I'd say it's been going on for about three months now.
